resources.string: Ready. Open any app and its text is translated in place.
Babel needs two permissions before it can translate.
Lets Babel read the text on screen. Translation runs for as long as this service is on.
Lets Babel draw the translation over the original text.
Pausing stops new text being translated. What is already on screen stays until the content changes. Manga mode is separate and keeps working.
Follows the system language. This is what text is translated into, not the language of this app.
Reads the screen as an image so text inside pictures can be translated. Uses the accessibility permission you have already granted.
Manga mode needs Android 11 or later and the Babel accessibility service switched on.
On-device translation is limited. A hosted model reads the whole balloon and translates it far better — but the text on your screen has to be sent to the service you name. Off unless you turn it on.
While this is on, recognised text leaves your device. Nothing else about Babel sends anything anywhere.
Saved key kept — leave blank to reuse it
Leave blank for a server on your own machine
Paste the authentication key from your DeepL account — nothing else. The address follows from the key, and a free-tier key is recognised by its :fx ending.
Any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, path included — usually ends in /v1/chat/completions. A hosted service must use https; a server of your own is reached over http on localhost.

Comic recogniser installed — lettering is read accurately.
Manga mode works now. Downloading the comic recogniser makes it read the lettering accurately instead of approximately.
